# iliad-133 — review, pass 1 (Iliad 21.97–199; units only, gloss.json not yet present)

Method: every note read against its line (labels, positions, cross-references); Greek → `l` → `i`; every house rendering checked against the Iliad table (`conventions.md`) and the Odyssey table; the neighbouring part's last unit (iliad-132, 21.95–96) checked for speech continuity: it closes Lycaon's plea with ”, so 21.97 correctly opens outside a speech. Quotation marks checked unit by unit: “ and `mark` on 99, 122, 150, 153, 184; ” on 111–113, 133–135, 151, 160, 198–199. All correct. Line division of `l` equals that of `t` in every unit. `t` untouched (verified by script against the original). No scansion flags in the packet; nothing to scan.

Severity: high = wrong sense or false claim; medium = table non-conformity or false label; low = polish.

## Findings considered and refused

- 167 · i "flew past above him": the Greek has only ὑπὲρ αὐτοῦ "above him"; "flew past" is inference, but it is the natural picture (cf. 21.69) and the note says the spear was over Achilles. Left.
- 122–123 · ἀκηδέες "uncaring" against the table's passive ἀκηδής "uncared for": the drafter's departure is justified (the word is active here, said of the fish) and the note now cites the Odyssey passage correctly. Left.
- 127 · ἀργέτα "white fat": confirmed by published iliad-071 (ἀργέτι δημῷ "white fat"); the table's "bright" is for ἀργῆτι of cloth and thunderbolts. Left.
- 178 · Αἰακίδαο `l` "descendant of Aeacus" / `i` "Achilles": follows the table; the note says who. Left.
- 192, 194 · κρείων "lord", χραισμεῖν "help", βαθυρρείταο "deep-flowing": all conform. Left.
- 125 · κόλπον "bosom", 132 · καθίετε "let down", 168 · ἐνεστήρικτο "fixed": no table row against them. Left.
- 136 · κηρόθι, 140 · ἐπᾶλτο, 169 · ἰθυπτίωνα, 190 · ἁλιμυρηέντων: new, hedged correctly in the notes where the sense is uncertain. Left.
- `about` uses "mightier" and "offspring": free prose, not `l`/`i`. Left.
- 111 · δείλη "evening" in `l`, "afternoon, evening" in the note: the note says the range, `l`/`i` pick "evening". Left.
- 114 · English of Odyssey 24.345 and 148–149 (= 20.176–177, iliad-128): checked word for word against the published units; identical.

# Pass 2 (units.json, gloss.json, new-renderings.md)

Method: fresh read of every unit against the packet lines (labels, positions, cross-references), Greek → `l` → `i`, house renderings re-checked against the tables, quotation marks and `mark` re-checked, then every `gloss.json` parse checked against its line. Script checks: `t` of every unit equals the packet lines in order and is unchanged from pass 1; `l` has as many line breaks as `t`; no straight quotes in `l`/`i`/`n`; “ and ” balanced and identical in `l` and `i` of every unit (open on 99, 122, 150, 153, 184; close on 111, 133, 151, 160, 198). No pass-1 change was reversed.

## Gloss parses checked and left

ὀρούσας (known entry “ὀρούω … aor. part.: ’springing’” covers 182; the lemma is ὀρούω, not ὄρνυμι); ἀπολιχμήσονται (fut. 3 pl. mid. of ἀπολιχμάομαι, αἷμα the object, σε … ὠτειλήν the accusative of whole and part); ὅρμηνεν (ὁρμαίνω, unaugmented, ν-movable; aorist-or-imperfect is not decided by the line and the translation is the same); the other __broaden__ entries (ἣ 167, ἄρῃ 112, κάλλιστον 158, κατ’ 172, κεῖσ’ 184, μέσον 111, ξάνθος 146, παισὶν 184, ἕληται 112, αὐχένα 116): each new piece is true of its line. κιχείομεν, κεχόλωτο, μεθῆκε, λύτο, σύτο, φάγῃσι, βάλῃσι, παύσειε, ἀντιόωσι, ἀρκέσει, ἐπέφνετε, ἐνεστήρικτο, ἰθυπτίωνα, ἁλιμυρηέντων checked against their lines: correct. All 93 novel forms have an entry; every entry is under 230 characters with typographic ’ only.

## Findings considered and refused

- 150 · ὅ in ὅ μευ ἔτλης: taken as the relative “who”; some take it as “that/because”. The unit’s English “who dared / you who dared” is the natural one and the known entry for ὅ is not broadened on a doubtful reading. Left.
- 176 · i “eased off his strength” and l “let go of his strength”: awkward but true to μεθῆκε βίης; no table row. Left.
- 115 · note “presumably the spear of Achilles that Lycaon had held (21.71)”: hedged, left.
- 126 · κατὰ κῦμα … φρῖχ’ ὑπαΐξει: the construction of the accusative φρῖχα with ὑπαΐξει is not certain; `l` “up through the dark ripple” and `i` “along the wave through the dark ripple” keep both words, the note does not claim more. Left.
- 167–168 · ἣ as the spear, feminine (ἐγχείη): the note says so; left.
- 162–163 · no verb: the note says so and the English supplies “threw” in `i` only. Left.

Brought into line with the final units.json: rows rewritten for ἀμείλικτον, ἐρύκακε, ἐνεστήρικτο λιλαιομένη, εὔχομαι, ἀνάσσων, ἰσοφαρίζει, σμαραγήσῃ, ἐπευχόμενος (the wrong “avoided: vaunting” removed), ἐρισθενέος Κρονίωνος, line 183 (ὀρούσας “springing”), σκότος ὄσσε κάλυψεν ἀσθμαίνοντ’ (“panting”), γένος/γενεή (“lineage”, 190 included), ἀκηδέες (Odyssey 20.130 now named as the Odyssey). Rows added for λισσόμενος, πιφαύσκεο, Ilios (104, 156) and sacred Ilium (128), ὀλοφύρεαι, ἀγαθοῖο, ξίφος ἄμφηκες, δεῦε, μίγη, ἀντίος, ἀντιόωσι, κλυτὸν ἔγχεϊ, ἐριζέμεναι, κρείσσων, χύντο, δεινὴν βροντήν, Διὶ Κρονίωνι. Not built, nothing committed.
